## Budget Planner with Daily Allowance | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/budget-planner.html
 FEATURE · BUDGETS · FREE + PRO
 A budget that starts on payday and knows what day it is.
 TrackExpenses lets your budget month start on any day from the 1st to the 31st, shows every budget bar with a marker for today, and — with Pro — turns what is left into a daily budget allowance, a forecast and what-if plans.

            Real app screens with example records.
 Your month, not the calendar's
 Paid on the 25th? Set More → Period & Entry to start on the 25th and every list, chart, budget and total runs from 25th to 24th. Days past the end of a short month are clamped, so “31” simply means the last day.
 Pacing, not just totals
 Sixty percent spent means nothing until you know where the month is. Every budget bar pairs the amount spent with a notch for today, so you can see at a glance whether you are ahead of or behind the month. Set a total budget and per-category budgets under More → Budgets, weekly, monthly or yearly.
 What Pro adds
   Daily budget allowance:  what is left, divided by the days left including today. If it reaches zero you see “Budget used up” — free, always.   Forecast:  where this period is heading at your current pace.   What-if plans:  try a daily target or a planned purchase and see the effect before you spend.
 Historical comparisons, averages and category changes stay free. Try the arithmetic without the app in the  daily budget calculator .
  Questions   Can the budget month start on my payday?  Yes. Choose any start day from 1 to 31 under More, Period and Entry. It applies to the whole ledger, not just one budget.    Is budgeting free?  Yes. Total and category budgets, the today marker and the payday month are free. Daily allowance, forecasts and what-if plans are Pro.    Does it support biweekly pay?  The setting is a fixed monthly start day. Weekly and yearly budget views exist, but there is no rolling two-week pay cycle.

## Expense Reports and Spending Insights | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/expense-reports.html
 FEATURE · REPORTS · FREE
 See where the money went, five different ways.
 TrackExpenses shows the same period as a daily list, a calendar, a month-by-month table, a summary and a by-description view, with stats for cash flow, daily average and the categories that changed most — all free.

            Real app screens with example records.
 The five lenses
   Daily:  every entry, grouped by day, with each day's total.   Calendar:  income and spending in a month grid; tap a day for its entries.   Monthly:  one row per period for the whole year, each with income, expenses and total.   Summary:  accounts and budget progress on one screen.   Description:  totals by payee, so recurring shops stand out.
 Stats that answer real questions
 Stats → Overview compares spending with the same point of the previous period, counts entries and the average per entry, names the top category, shows cash flow (income minus expenses), your average per calendar day and how many days had no spending. “What changed?” lists the categories that moved most; tap one to see its entries. Switch between weekly, monthly and yearly units.
 Filter, search, export
 Filter any lens by income, expense or transfer and by category — the totals strip always describes the same filtered set. Search finds any entry. Export the selected month to CSV for free; Pro adds any date range, CSV import and full JSON backup.
  Questions   Are the reports free?  Yes. All five transaction views, Stats overview, category changes, search and filters are free.    Can I export to Excel or Numbers?  Yes. Export the selected month to CSV for free and open it in Numbers, Excel or Google Sheets. Date-range exports are Pro.

## Multi-Currency Expense Tracker for iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/multi-currency-expense-tracker.html
 FEATURE · CURRENCIES · FREE
 Spend in any currency. Read one total.
 TrackExpenses records each transaction in the currency you paid in, with the exchange rate you choose, and converts every total, budget and account balance into one main currency — so a trip abroad doesn’t break your month.

         Real app screens with example records.
 How it works
   Pick a main currency  under More → Main Currency. Every total is reported in it.   Add the currencies you use  under More → Additional Currencies.   Log in the currency you paid.  The entry sheet asks for the rate to your main currency and prefills the last rate you used for that currency.
 Accounts can hold money in their own currency, such as a USD travel account. The Accounts screen converts each balance into your main currency using the rate each entry was made at, and says so on screen.
 Why your own rate
 TrackExpenses doesn't fetch live rates from the internet. The rate your bank or card actually charged is the true one, and it often differs from a market rate. A foreign entry can't be saved without a rate, because saving it at 1 would quietly distort that currency's history.
 Built for
  Travel spending in several countries.  Expats paid in one currency and sending money home in another.  Bank alerts in foreign currencies: imported purchases wait for their rate instead of guessing.
  Questions   Does TrackExpenses update exchange rates automatically?  No. You enter the rate, prefilled from the last one you used for that currency. This keeps the figures equal to what your bank actually charged.    Is multi-currency a Pro feature?  No. Main and additional currencies are part of the free ledger.
  More features   Say it voice entry  Bank SMS import  Budgets, pacing & payday month  Reports, calendar & insights  Accounts, cards & recurring  Widgets, Quick Add & Shortcuts  Private by design

## Accounts, Credit Cards and Recurring Bills | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/accounts-and-transfers.html
 FEATURE · ACCOUNTS · 3 FREE
 Every account, every transfer, no double counting.
 TrackExpenses tracks cash, bank, card, savings, investment and loan accounts, records transfers between them, and shows assets, liabilities and a total that always reconcile. Recurring rules add your salary, rent and subscriptions on schedule.

         Real app screens with example records.
 Transfers are not spending
 Withdrawing cash, moving money to savings or paying off a credit card moves money between places you own. TrackExpenses records those as transfers, so the lunch you later buy with that cash is counted once. Bank SMS imports recognize ATM withdrawals, cash deposits and card bill payments and file them as transfers when both accounts are clear.
 Credit cards
 A card account carries what you owe as a liability. Purchases on the card are expenses; the monthly payment is a transfer from your bank to the card. Read the  credit card guide  for the full method.
 Recurring transactions
 More → Recurring creates rules every day, week, month or year — or every N of them, such as every 2 weeks. Each occurrence is created once, even when two of your devices sync.
 Safe with history
 An account with history is archived rather than deleted, so past balances still add up. A deleted transaction can be undone for a few seconds, everywhere in the app.
 Free or Pro
 Free includes 3 accounts and 3 recurring rules. Pro makes both unlimited.
  Questions   How do I record paying my credit card bill?  Record it as a transfer from your bank account to the card account, not as an expense. The purchases on the card were already your spending.    Can I have more than three accounts?  Free covers three accounts, for example cash, bank and one card. Pro allows unlimited accounts.
  Step-by-step guides    Credit Card Payment vs Expense: Avoid Double Counting    Track Subscriptions and Recurring Bills on iPhone      More features   Say it voice entry  Bank SMS import  Budgets, pacing & payday month  Reports, calendar & insights  Multi-currency  Widgets, Quick Add & Shortcuts  Private by design

 Log an expense without opening the app.

         Real app screens with example records.
 Widgets
   Budget:  what is left to spend this period — Home Screen and Lock Screen sizes.   Spending Overview:  today's spending and the period's income and expenses.   Quick Add:  add an expense by typing, voice or a bank message; a Lock Screen microphone opens Say it.
 Control Center
 On iOS 18 and later, add  Say an Expense  and  Paste an Expense  to Control Center or the Lock Screen. Copy a bank alert, swipe down, tap Paste an Expense and the draft is ready.

 Actions include Log an Expense, Log Income, Say an Expense, Paste an Expense, Budget Remaining, Import Bank Message and Import Wallet Transaction. Ask Siri “What's left in TrackExpenses”, or build a Wallet automation that logs Apple Pay purchases on selected cards (see the  Apple Pay guide ).

 A money app that never asks for your bank password.
 TrackExpenses has no bank connection and no app account. Your ledger lives on your device, with optional sync through your own private iCloud, and App Lock protects it with a passcode and Face ID.

         Real app screens with example records.
 What stays where
   No bank login:  entries come from you, your voice, or messages you choose to pass in through Shortcuts.   No account:  nothing to sign up for; no email required. Messages aren't kept:  an imported alert is read and discarded; only the transaction is saved.   Voice stays local:  speech is recognized on the device.

 Who it suits

## Privacy Policy | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/privacy.html
 Privacy Policy
  Expense Tracker: SMS & Voice (TrackExpenses)  — last updated 5 October 2026.
 The short version
 TrackExpenses has no account, no login, and no server of ours. Your ledger lives on your iPhone, and — if you leave iCloud on — in your own private iCloud database. We cannot see it, and neither can anyone else.
 What TrackExpenses stores

 The ledger you build: transactions with their amount, currency, date, category, account, payee and any note you write.
 Your accounts, account groups and their balances, your budgets, and your recurring rules.
 The categories you keep or create.
 Your settings: the day your fiscal month starts, your main and additional currencies, your reminder time, your app icon, and whether the app lock is on.

 Where it is stored
 On your device, in the app's own container. If iCloud is on for TrackExpenses, the same data syncs through  your private iCloud database  — that is Apple's infrastructure inside your Apple Account,  not a server of ours . We have no key to it, no console for it, and no way to read it. Turning iCloud off for TrackExpenses in your iOS settings keeps everything on the one device.
 Deleting the app removes the copy on that device. There is no copy on any server of ours, because there is no server of ours.
 What leaves your device
  Purchases.  TrackExpenses uses RevenueCat to manage subscriptions and restore purchases. When you buy, restore, or open the paywall, RevenueCat receives purchase and receipt information, an anonymous app user ID it generates, a device identifier, and basic app and OS version details. This is used to work out whether you have an active subscription, and nothing else. It is not used for advertising, and it is not shared with data brokers. RevenueCat's own policy is at  https://www.revenuecat.com/privacy .
  Apple.  Purchases are processed by Apple under Apple's own privacy policy, and iCloud sync is carried by Apple under your Apple Account. We never see your payment details.
 That is the complete list. The app makes no network requests of its own. There is no analytics SDK, no advertising SDK, no crash reporter, and no third-party tracking of any kind in it.
 TrackExpenses never connects to your bank
 There is no bank login, no account aggregator, and no place to type a banking credential. TrackExpenses knows your balances because you told it, and for no other reason. It cannot move money, and it cannot see an account you have not entered yourself.
 SMS auto-import is not access to your messages
 iOS never hands an app your Messages inbox, and TrackExpenses does not ask for it. The optional SMS auto-import is a  Shortcuts automation that you set up and control : when a bank alert arrives, Shortcuts passes that one message's text to the app. The optional Apple Pay import works the same way through a Shortcuts Transaction automation, which hands the app the amount, the merchant and the card's name, and nothing else.
 It is read on your device. Only the amount, the merchant, the date and the last digits of the card the message names reach your ledger — as a transaction you can edit or delete like any other, marked as imported until you have looked at it. The message text itself is  never saved . Two small records are kept on the device so you can see the automation working: a short numeric fingerprint of each message for up to 24 hours, purely so that a retried automation cannot enter the same purchase twice, and an activity log of what each run did — the time, the outcome, and the amount and payee that reached your ledger, never the message. If you turn on import notifications, the app posts them locally. Nothing about the message leaves your device, and deleting the automation in Shortcuts ends the whole arrangement.
 You can also paste a bank message in yourself, on the new-transaction screen. It is read on the same terms: on your device, into a draft you check before saving, with the message text  never stored . On an iPhone with Apple Intelligence, a message the app's own rules cannot read is passed to Apple's on-device model so that banks and languages the app was never taught can still be understood — that model runs on your iPhone, and the message does not leave it.
 Voice entry runs on your device
 Speech is recognised on your iPhone by Apple's on-device speech and Apple Intelligence models. Audio is streamed straight to the recogniser as you speak — it is  never written to a file , never stored, and never uploaded — and it is discarded as soon as the draft transaction appears. What voice entry produces is a draft you confirm, not an entry made behind your back.
 Things people reasonably assume, that aren't true here

  TrackExpenses does not access your contacts, your photos, your location, or any other app.
  Face ID / Touch ID.  If you turn on the app lock, authentication is handled entirely by iOS. TrackExpenses is told only whether it succeeded. Your biometric data never reaches the app.
  Notifications  are scheduled locally on your device. Nothing is sent through a server.
  The widget and the Siri shortcuts  read a small summary from a shared container on your device only.

 Tracking
 TrackExpenses  does not track you . It does not link your data with third-party data for advertising, and it does not share data with data brokers. It never requests the advertising identifier.
 Your data, your control

  Export.  The Transactions screen exports the month you are viewing as a CSV for spreadsheets. This is free, and stays free, so your records are never locked in. With TrackExpenses Pro, More → Backup & Export also exports any date range and writes a full-fidelity JSON backup of everything the app holds, which it can restore. You choose where each file goes; nothing is uploaded.
  Import.  With Pro, More → Backup & Export also reads a CSV file you pick — from a spreadsheet, another money app, or a bank. The file is read entirely on your device, you see exactly what it would add before anything is written, and nothing about it is uploaded. TrackExpenses only ever sees the one file you hand it.
  Delete.  Deleting the app removes its data from that device. To remove the synced copy, delete the app's iCloud data from your iOS settings under your Apple Account. For the purchase record Apple and RevenueCat hold, email us and we will request its deletion on your behalf.

 Children
 TrackExpenses is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect any information from children under 13.
 Not financial advice
 TrackExpenses is a record-keeping tool. Its insights — safe-to-spend, projected spending, comparisons against last period — are arithmetic on the numbers you entered. They are  not financial advice , and they are only ever as accurate as what you have recorded.
 Changes
 If this policy changes, the date at the top changes with it, and material changes will be noted in the app's release notes.
 Contact
 Questions about privacy, or a deletion request:  atabany.apps@gmail.com

## Daily Budget Until Payday Calculator | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/daily-budget.html
 What is left to spend per day?
 Subtract spending and any extra commitments from your period budget, then divide by the days left, including today. This is budget arithmetic; an unrecorded bill or purchase can change the answer.
  Daily budget until payday  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Use one currency for every amount.
   Period budget    Recorded spending    Extra upcoming commitments   Only commitments not already in recorded spending.   Today's date    Last day of this budget period   Usually the day before your next payday.    Calculate daily budget
 Example: 1,200 − 480 − 120 = 600 remaining. Over 10 days including today, that is 60.00 per day.   JavaScript enables the calculator. Use the formula and table below without it; all guides and examples remain readable.
 Reference examples    Illustrative amounts in one currency; remaining days include today    Budget  Spent  Extra commitments  Days left  Per day      1,200  480  120  10  60.00    1,200  600  0  15  40.00    900  850  50  5  0.00    900  950  0  5  0.00 (50 over budget)    600  420  0  1  180.00
 The formula and its limits   Daily amount = max(0, budget − recorded spending − extra commitments) ÷ days left.  We include today and the last day. A period ending today has one day left. A date in the past produces an error instead of an invented allowance. The display rounds to two decimal places; the calculation keeps the unrounded result.  Only subtract extra commitments once. If next week's rent is already included in recorded spending, leave it out of the extra-commitments field. This calculator offers an optional reserve you choose; it is not an exact replica of every TrackExpenses forecasting scenario.  From an example to your ledger  TrackExpenses lets your month start on a fixed monthly payday and keeps transactions, budgets and charts in the same window. Ordinary budget facts and pacing stay free. Pro adds daily guidance, forecasts and what-if plans based on your recorded figures.   Set your monthly payday period  ·  Check recorded spending in CSV
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated October 2026 ·  Suggest a correction


## Best iPhone Expense Trackers: How to Choose
https://trackexpenses.app/compare/best-expense-trackers.html
 Choose an iPhone expense tracker by workflow.
 The best expense tracker for you is the one whose entry method you will keep using. Compare how you add purchases, how periods work and where your data goes before choosing by a feature count.  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated October 2026 ·  Suggest a correction
 This is the developer's comparison on the TrackExpenses website. It is not an independent ranking. The table reports features checked in each product's own documentation; “—” means unverified here, not absent.
   Documented workflows checked 5 October 2026    App  Entry / automation  Month or budget window  Useful distinction      TrackExpenses  Manual, optional SMS/Wallet Shortcuts, Pro voice drafts  Fixed monthly start for ledger, budgets and charts  No app account/bank login; on-device voice; free monthly CSV     Monefy   Manual income and expense tracking  First day of month, 1–31, can follow payroll  A documented custom-month option; SMS/voice —     Monetal   SMS/email recognition documented for iOS  Flexible budgets documented; full report scope —  Offline operation and no registration; voice —     Tab.it   iOS SMS Shortcuts setup  —  Its setup uses a token connected to a Tab.it account     Spendee   Entry/connection modes depend on chosen workflow  Budget start date and daily allowance documented  Check whether the budget window matches the reports you need     Cash Book   Voice, including multiple transactions per sentence  —  Voice documentation describes a relay to an AI model and a connection requirement
 If your bank sends useful SMS alerts  TrackExpenses, Monetal and Tab.it document iOS message workflows. Compare setup, format handling, review and privacy. SMS tracking is not exclusive to one app, and none of these documented workflows proves that your particular bank format will work. Test a real alert before relying on automation.  If you prefer to say purchases  Compare supported languages, device requirements and whether audio is processed locally or remotely. TrackExpenses makes on-device drafts with Pro on compatible devices; Cash Book documents a connected processing route. The right choice depends on the devices and languages you actually use.  If payday is your month boundary  TrackExpenses and Monefy both document custom monthly starts. Spendee documents a budget start date and daily allowance. A date option alone does not establish that every list and chart follows it: inspect the report scope you need. TrackExpenses applies its fiscal month to the ledger, budgets and charts.  Try a small real ledger  Add one expense, one income and a transfer between accounts. Check a payday boundary, export a sample and inspect the privacy policy. Those actions show whether the workflow fits you better than an unsupported claim that one app is “best” for everyone. ## Monefy Alternative with SMS and Voice | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/compare/monefy-alternative.html
 A Monefy alternative for SMS and voice entry.  Consider TrackExpenses if you want optional bank SMS imports and on-device voice drafts alongside a fixed monthly payday budget. Monefy already documents a custom first day of month, so payday reporting alone is not a reason to switch.  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated October 2026 ·  Suggest a correction   This page is written by TrackExpenses' developer. It compares documented workflows and does not claim to have tested every Monefy feature.
  When to keep Monefy  ·  When to try TrackExpenses  ·  Check your data first
 When to keep Monefy  If you are comfortable with manual entry and Monefy already gives you the records you need, there may be little value in moving. Its  official help  documents a first-day-of-month setting from 1 to 31, including aligning the month with payroll. A familiar entry habit is valuable.  When to try TrackExpenses  Try it when logging is the part you struggle to maintain. Optional Shortcuts automations pass supported bank alerts or Wallet purchases into the ledger. The app does not read your Messages inbox and does not need a bank login. With Pro, one spoken sentence can become several on-device drafts that you review before saving.  The free ledger includes budgets, historical stats, monthly CSV export and private iCloud sync, with 3 accounts, 3 recurring rules and 20 successful automatic bank SMS imports per calendar month per device. Pro adds forecasts/daily guidance, unlimited SMS imports/accounts/rules, voice and flexible import/export. Device and language support apply to voice.  Check your data before moving  Keep an original copy of your old records. Do not assume a CSV's columns have the same meanings in another app. TrackExpenses Pro previews CSV import and lets you map columns, but this page does not promise that every Monefy export is compatible. Test a small sample and check date, amount, currency, category and direction before confirming a larger import.  Account transfers are especially important to check: a move between your own accounts should not become a new purchase. A change of app should improve your workflow while preserving your understanding of the figures.  Compare a week of ordinary use  Try the same three or four real tasks: record a cash expense, review a bank alert, browse your payday month and export records. Keep the tool that makes those tasks easiest for you. No website comparison can measure that personal fit in advance.
